title: Coefficient-unit component of finite direct-image comparison
statement:
theorem diagonalTrace_finitePush_unit (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l X] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l S]
    {f : X ⟶ S} (p : Presentation l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) f) (n : ℕ) :
    let E := ULift.{u} (Padic l)
    let evS := ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (DiagonalMod l S)).obj (op n)).mapDerivedCategory
    p.finitePushUnit l ≫
        p.Rf.R.map (p.coefficientsX.unitMap l E p.LX ≫ (p.LX.projection n).app _) ≫
        (p.finitePushComparison l n).hom.app (SpTowerClasses.unit X
          (SpTowerClasses.Arings l E X)) =
      (p.coefficientsS.unitMap l E p.LS ≫ (p.LS.projection n).app _) ≫
        evS.map (p.restrictionS.F.mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((SpTowerShriek.adjunction l E p.base p.model.geometry).homEquiv _ _
            (p.model.coefficientPullback.derivedIso l E).hom))

proof.text: The ordinary completed-to-finite coefficient projections and direct-image unit form a commutative square: both coefficient ring maps are the unital finite quotient maps at exponent n+1. The coefficient-pullback normalization fixes the geometric unit component.

Use the exact-cone projection identity and full common-unit normalization of the completed and evaluation squares. The varying normalization on K-injectives extends to the relevant natural transformation by right-derived-functor uniqueness. The derived adjunction on single objects identifies the geometric coefficient adjunct with its ordinary adjunct followed by the underived-to-derived direct-image unit. Transport the ordinary unital square, then cancel the single-object and varying comparisons.
